categories.title: Emergent Spacetime, Fractal Folding & Quantum Gravity

publications.title: Towards a Geometric Interpretation of Electron Spin: A Research Programme on 360° Periodicity, Internal Topology, and Superconducting Pairing
publications.abstract: We propose a geometric research programme re-examining the carrier of the electron's rotational phase. We conjecture that the electron possesses an intrinsic internal geometry for which a 360° rotation constitutes a complete topological event, with conventional 720° periodicity reflecting global spinor representation topology. Furthermore, this internal geometry provides a geometric descriptor for Cooper pair topology in superconductors, complementing the BCS mechanism.

publications.title: Information Fractal Geometry (IFG): A Geometry-First Reconstruction of the HTSIE Framework (v1.0)
publications.abstract: Reconstructs the IFG framework centered on the Information Accessibility Transition (IAT). Proves that gravitational compression (UV) and cosmological dilution (IR) flow toward the same geometric fixed point—the Boundary Encoding Phase (BEP)—under RG analysis.

publications.title: Information Folding Geometry (IFG) Phase 1: Self-Consistency Analysis and Dimensional Hierarchy
publications.abstract: Analyzes the dimensional hierarchy (0D → 3D) using Fisher information volume. Resolves topological obstructions of the Information Folding Operator F by recasting it as a morphism in Whitney-stratified spaces or Lagrangian correspondences.

publications.title: The Hidden Thread of Structural Information Evolution: A Comparative Study of Condensed Matter, Quantum Plasma and Black Hole Systems
publications.abstract: Proposes a unified framework linking condensed matter, quantum plasma, and black holes. Shows that energy storage migrates from particle kinetics to boundary encoding, unifying the Chandrasekhar, TOV, and Bekenstein limits as expressions of a single information principle.

publications.title: Invariant Light-Cone Algebra and Emergent Causal Structure
publications.abstract: Formulates a pre-geometric algebra where light speed invariance emerges from a primitive C*-algebraic structure rather than a spacetime postulate.

publications.title: Fractal Folding Theory: From the Kakeya Conjecture to Quantum Gravity Observations
publications.abstract: Links the Wang-Zahl (2025) 3D Kakeya set proof to Planck-scale spacetime folding dynamics. Computes spectral dimension scaling via RBN simulations and provides observable predictions for black hole echo delays (τ₀ ≈ 355 μs).

publications.title: Time as Irreversible Spectral-Dimension Flow with a 1/3 Power Law
publications.abstract: Proposes time as an emergent property of spatial spectral dimension flow (Ds: 3 → 2). Replaces the Big Bang singularity with a smooth cosmological bounce and yields falsifiable predictions for sub-millimeter fifth-force experiments.

publications.title: Spectral Dimension Flow, Horizon Defects, and Emergent Time
publications.abstract: Models the black hole horizon as a localized non-orientable Möbius-type defect under metric scale transformations, deriving covariant emergent time via causal cone collapse.

publications.title: Sun's (2,4,6,8) Binomial Representation Program: Multi-Kernel Computational Verification, Modular Radar Audits, and Chunk-Level Lean 4 Formalization
publications.abstract: Computational verification of the candidate counterexample n* = 896,315,812,331,399 to Sun's (2,4,6,8) binomial representation conjecture (OEIS A306477). Reports 12 independent verification kernels, modular radar audits, and chunk-level Lean 4 kernel verification.

publications.title: A Computational Audit of a Candidate Counterexample to Sun's (2,4,6,8) Conjecture — Version 23.4: Exhaustive Verification and Cantor-Pascal Diagnostics
publications.abstract: Exhaustive computational audit of the candidate counterexample n* = 896,315,812,331,399 to Sun's (2,4,6,8) binomial representation conjecture. Enumerates all 2,818,953,028 admissible triples and introduces Cantor-Pascal diagnostic framework.

publications.title: Möbius–Lorentz Quotients and Null Pin Holonomy: Affine Normal Forms, Null-Displacement Loci, Mapping-Torus Topology, Pin Lifts, and Mirror-Residue Pairing
publications.abstract: Develops a rigorous mathematical framework for Lorentzian Möbius-type quotients and null pin holonomy, establishing seven theorems on affine normal forms, null-displacement loci, topology, and mirror-residue pairing.

title: Why the Past May Be Physically Inaccessible: A Theoretical Review and Compatibility Framework
abstract: Formulates the Historical Information Accessibility Problem (HIAP): whether a macroscopic physical system can be consistently re-embedded into an earlier epoch without violating geometric, quantum, causal, thermodynamic, and historical-information consistency conditions. Introduces Historical Exchange Asymmetry (HXA) as a new conceptual layer.
